section: Measurement of unemployment - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS; PLFS methodology and recent findings
subsections: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS
Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds
Key labour indicators - LFPR, WPR, UR
Agencies and sources of unemployment data

accepted.s: Under the Usual Principal Status approach, a person is treated as employed when the person has worked for the major part of the reference period. What is the relevant reference period and minimum duration?
o: Each day and 4 hours of work
accepted.x: UPS uses a reference period of 365 days. A person is considered employed if the major part of the year, generally 183 days or more, was spent working.
accepted.tq: Match the reference period with the qualifying duration.
accepted.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Usual Principal and Subsidiary Status approach?
o: It counts only persons working for 183 days or more in a year.
It counts a person as employed if work was performed for four hours on any day.
It includes principal-status workers and those undertaking subsidiary work for at least 30 days in the year.
It counts a person as employed only if work was performed on each day of the reference week.
accepted.x: UPSS includes persons employed under principal status as well as those who performed subsidiary work for at least 30 days during the 365-day reference period.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between principal-status and subsidiary-status conditions.
accepted.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the Current Daily Status approach, the basic time unit used for recording employment is:
accepted.x: CDS uses a half-day as the unit of measurement. Four or more hours of work are treated as employment for that day.
accepted.tq: Test the precise quantitative unit used in a statistical approach.
accepted.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A person worked for five hours on one day and remained without work on the other days of the reference week. Under which approach would the person be treated as employed for that day?
accepted.x: Under CDS, four or more hours of work count as employment for the day. The approach records employment and unemployment for each day of the seven-day period.
accepted.tq: Apply the qualifying-hour rule to a short employment situation.
accepted.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Why does the Current Daily Status approach generally produce the highest unemployment rate?
o: It counts days of unemployment even for persons treated as employed under CWS.
It uses a reference period of 365 days.
It includes only persons who are not seeking work.
It excludes all seasonal workers from employment.
accepted.x: CDS records unemployment separately for each day and therefore captures intermittent unemployment that may not be reflected when a person is counted as employed under CWS.
accepted.tq: Identify the cause behind a comparison in measured unemployment rates.
accepted.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an unemployment measurement approach used in the listed status-based framework?
accepted.x: Current Monthly Status is not one of the listed NSS status approaches. UPS, CWS and CDS are recognised approaches in this framework.
accepted.tq: Find the non-method inserted among closely related statistical methods.
accepted.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Census terminology, which combination is correctly matched?
o: Main worker — worked for less than 183 days in a year
Marginal worker — worked for 183 days or more in a year
Main worker — worked for 183 days or more in a year
Main worker — worked only for one hour during the reference week
accepted.x: The Census classifies a person who worked for 183 days or more in a year as a main worker. A person working for less than 183 days is a marginal worker.
accepted.tq: Separate Census worker categories from NSS status approaches.
accepted.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The unemployment rates under UPS, CWS and CDS in the NSS 68th Round for 2011–12 were respectively:
accepted.x: For 2011–12, the NSS 68th Round reported unemployment rates of 2.7% under UPS, 3.7% under CWS and 5.6% under CDS.
accepted.tq: Recall the ordered numerical series and preserve the approach sequence.
accepted.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was the last quinquennial round of the National Sample Survey relating to employment and unemployment?
accepted.x: The NSS 68th Round for 2011–12 was the last quinquennial employment-unemployment round before the PLFS system became the regular source of such estimates.
accepted.tq: Identify the terminal item in a sequence of survey rounds.
accepted.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The unemployment rate for persons aged 15 years and above in the first PLFS, conducted for 2017–18, was:
accepted.x: The first PLFS, for 2017–18, reported an unemployment rate of 6.1% for persons aged 15 years and above.
accepted.tq: Link the first survey year with its reported headline rate.
accepted.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: PLFS 2022–23 reported an overall unemployment rate of 3.2%, while the rate for graduates was 13%. The other year-rate combinations are incorrect.
accepted.tq: Match each survey year with its distinctive rate or finding.
accepted.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about PLFS 2023–24:
1. The overall unemployment rate under UPSS was 3.2%.
2. The rural unemployment rate was lower than the urban rate.
3. The urban unemployment rate was 5.1%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The urban rate was 5.1%, while the rural rate was 2.5%, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Compare the overall, rural and urban figures before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the monthly CWS unemployment rates for March, April and May 2026, respectively?
accepted.x: The monthly CWS rates were 5.1% in March 2026, 5.2% in April 2026 and 5.5% in May 2026.
accepted.tq: Preserve the chronological order of closely spaced monthly figures.
accepted.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The quarterly CWS unemployment rate for January–March 2026, along with the urban and rural rates, was:
accepted.x: For January–March 2026, the quarterly CWS unemployment rate was 5.0%; the urban rate was 6.6% and the rural rate was 4.3%.
accepted.tq: Match the aggregate figure with its two geographical components.
accepted.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As reported by CMIE, approximately how many persons were unemployed in India in December 2021?
accepted.x: CMIE reported approximately 53 million unemployed persons as of December 2021.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive large-scale numerical estimate associated with a private agency.
accepted.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the CMIE estimate from official PLFS figures?
o: CMIE conducts the quinquennial NSS employment-unemployment rounds.
CMIE reports only decennial Census worker data.
CMIE is a private source and its unemployment rate was about 7.95% in September 2023, higher than the official PLFS figures.
CMIE is a government survey and generally reports lower unemployment than PLFS.
accepted.x: CMIE is a private source. Its unemployment rate was approximately 7.95% in September 2023, higher than the corresponding official PLFS figures.
accepted.tq: Separate private and official sources using agency and trend clues.
accepted.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey is conducted by:
o: The Census of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs
The National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
The Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy under NITI Aayog
The Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
accepted.x: PLFS is conducted by the National Statistical Office, which functions under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
accepted.tq: Apply the 'who conducts the survey?' agency test.
accepted.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics was set up on the advice of which body and was associated with the design of PLFS?
accepted.x: The Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics was set up on the advice of the National Statistical Commission and designed the PLFS framework.
accepted.tq: Match the technical committee with the institution that recommended it.
accepted.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey was launched in:
accepted.x: PLFS was launched in April 2017. Its first annual report, relating to 2017–18, was released in May 2019.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the launch date from the release date of the first report.
accepted.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the original design of PLFS?
o: Only decennial rural estimates under UPS
Quarterly estimates for all areas under CDS alone
Annual rural and urban estimates under UPSS and CWS, with quarterly urban CWS estimates
Monthly all-India CDS estimates and annual urban estimates only
accepted.x: The original PLFS design provided annual rural and urban estimates under UPSS and CWS, along with quarterly CWS estimates for urban areas.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete original survey design.
accepted.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following changes was introduced with the PLFS revamp from January 2025?
1. Monthly all-India CWS estimates began to be produced.
2. Quarterly estimates were extended to rural areas.
3. The annual report shifted to the calendar year January–December.
4. The sample was reduced to about one-half of its earlier size.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The sample was raised, not reduced, to about 2,72,304 households.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the direction of a sample-size change.
accepted.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After the January 2025 revamp, the PLFS sample was raised to approximately:
accepted.x: The revised PLFS sample was raised to approximately 2,72,304 households, described as about 2.65 times the earlier size.
accepted.tq: Test the exact sample-size figure rather than the approximate multiplier alone.
accepted.sec: PLFS - agency, launch, frequency  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following persons would ordinarily be outside the labour force?
o: A student or homemaker not seeking work
A person unemployed but available for work
accepted.x: Persons who are not seeking work and are not available for work, such as some students and homemakers, are outside the labour force.
accepted.tq: Apply the condition of seeking or being available for work.
accepted.sec: Key labour indicators - LFPR, WPR, UR  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Unemployment Rate is calculated as:
o: Employed persons divided by total population multiplied by 100
Unemployed persons divided by labour force multiplied by 100
Unemployed persons divided by total population multiplied by 100
Labour force divided by total population multiplied by 100
accepted.x: UR measures the unemployed as a percentage of the labour force, not of the entire population. The latter denominator is used for Proportion Unemployed.
accepted.tq: Separate unemployment rate from proportion unemployed by checking the denominator.
accepted.sec: Key labour indicators - LFPR, WPR, UR  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which agency conducted the quinquennial Employment–Unemployment rounds from the 27th to the 68th Round and has conducted PLFS since 2017?
accepted.x: The NSSO, now within the NSO, conducted the quinquennial employment-unemployment rounds and became the institutional source for PLFS from 2017.
accepted.tq: Match the historical survey series with its responsible agency.
accepted.sec: Agencies and sources of unemployment data  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which organisation conducts the Employment–Unemployment Survey and the Quarterly Employment Survey of establishments?
o: Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
Directorate General of Employment and Training alone
accepted.x: The Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment conducts the Employment–Unemployment Survey and the Quarterly Employment Survey of establishments.
accepted.tq: Use the survey title to identify the responsible labour institution.
accepted.sec: Agencies and sources of unemployment data  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. CMIE — monthly household survey through CPHS
2. DGE&T/Employment Exchanges — registration data of job seekers
3. Census of India — main and marginal worker data every ten years
4. CSO — merged with NSSO into NSO in 2019
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. CMIE conducts the CPHS, Employment Exchanges provide registration data, Census supplies decennial worker data, and CSO and NSSO were merged into NSO in 2019.
accepted.tq: Verify each agency-role relationship before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Agencies and sources of unemployment data  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Before the establishment of NITI Aayog, unemployment data were primarily obtained from:
accepted.x: Before NITI Aayog, unemployment data were primarily obtained from the NSSO. Official unemployment information was also associated with the CSO and NSSO statistical system.
accepted.tq: Recall the principal historical source rather than a newer private source.
accepted.sec: Agencies and sources of unemployment data  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement about CMIE and PLFS is correct?
o: PLFS is a private survey and CMIE is conducted by MoSPI.
CMIE designs PLFS through the Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics.
CMIE is a private monthly household-survey source, whereas PLFS is the standard NSO mechanism.
Both are decennial official Census exercises.
accepted.x: CMIE conducts a private monthly household survey through CPHS. PLFS, conducted by NSO, is the standard official mechanism for measuring unemployment in India.
accepted.tq: Compare agency status, frequency and official character.
accepted.sec: Agencies and sources of unemployment data  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to PLFS 2023–24, the overall unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh under UPSS was:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded an overall unemployment rate of 4.1% under UPSS in PLFS 2023–24, compared with 3.2% for India.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the State figure from the corresponding national figure.
accepted.sec: AP unemployment rate in PLFS

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh under PLFS 2023–24:
1. The unemployment rate for youth aged 15–29 was 17.5%.
2. The rural youth unemployment rate was 15.5%.
3. The urban youth unemployment rate was 22.7%.
4. The urban female youth unemployment rate was 29.1%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct for Andhra Pradesh under PLFS 2023–24. The national youth unemployment rate given for comparison was 10.2%.
accepted.tq: Check all State-level subcategories before selecting the complete code.
accepted.sec: AP unemployment rate in PLFS

accepted.s: The Labour Force Participation Rate and Worker Population Ratio of Andhra Pradesh reported in the relevant PLFS-based State estimates were respectively:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded an LFPR of 47.5% and a WPR of 45.6%. LFPR is higher because it includes both employed and unemployed persons in the labour force.
accepted.tq: Preserve the indicator order and distinguish LFPR from WPR.
accepted.sec: AP unemployment rate in PLFS

accepted.s: Which one of the following comparisons is correct for PLFS 2023–24?
o: Andhra Pradesh overall unemployment was 4.1%, higher than India’s 3.2%.
India recorded 4.1%, while Andhra Pradesh recorded 3.2%.
Andhra Pradesh overall unemployment was lower than India’s rate.
Andhra Pradesh and India both recorded 5.9%.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded 4.1%, while the all-India rate was 3.2%. Thus, the State rate was higher than the national rate.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap carefully when comparing State and national figures.
accepted.sec: AP unemployment rate in PLFS

accepted.s: The Dantwala Committee on unemployment estimates was constituted in:
accepted.x: The Expert Committee on Unemployment Estimates, popularly known as the Dantwala Committee, was constituted in 1970.
accepted.tq: Separate the years of closely related employment committees.
accepted.sec: Committees on employment statistics

accepted.s: What was the principal recommendation of the Dantwala Committee regarding unemployment estimation?
o: To replace NSS surveys with CMIE surveys
To provide separate estimates by status and by category
To use one single national number for all forms of unemployment
accepted.x: The Dantwala Committee rejected a single-number estimate and recommended separate estimates by usual, weekly and daily status, as well as by category.
accepted.tq: Identify the committee recommendation that rejects an over-simplified single measure.
accepted.sec: Committees on employment statistics

accepted.s: Which committee reviewed unemployment estimates and employment-oriented policies in 1973?
o: Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics
accepted.x: The Bhagwati Committee, constituted in 1973, reviewed unemployment estimates and employment-oriented policies.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with its year and subject of review.
accepted.sec: Committees on employment statistics

accepted.s:
Consider the following committees or bodies:
1. Dantwala Committee — separate unemployment estimates by usual, weekly and daily status
2. Bhagwati Committee — employment-oriented policies
3. Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics — design of PLFS
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The Dantwala Committee dealt with status-wise estimates, the Bhagwati Committee reviewed employment policies, and SCLFS designed PLFS.
accepted.tq: Match each committee or body with its distinctive institutional role.
accepted.sec: Committees on employment statistics
